newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Norilsk says gas supply cuts dent output.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Norilsk says gas supply cuts dent output.

text.p: Gas supply cuts to Russian metal group Norilsk Nickel's flagship metals combine are hitting metals production, group spokesman Sergei Vetchinin said on Friday.

"I can say one thing, and that is that without doubt the gas supply cuts are affecting output (at the combine)," Vetchinin told Reuters. He added it was too early to say how much output was being lost due to lower energy supplies.

Natural gas supplies to RAO Norilsky Nikel's main production complex were cut by nearly one third last week over unpaid gas debts. Norilskgazprom, the supplier to the combine, said it had cut supplies to 11 million cubic metres a day from 16 million.

Vetchinin said Norilsk Nickel was partly compensating gas supply losses by switching to other fuels. He also said less gas was needed during the summer months to heat the Arctic town of Norilsk where the combine is situated.

"But we can't work under the current compensatory system for long," he said. Norilsk officials had held talks with Norilskgazprom to try to resolve the issue, but there were no clear signs yet that the gas supplier would change its policy towards Norilsk Nickel soon, he said.

Norilsk Nickel is one of the world's biggest suppliers of nickel, cobalt, platinum and palladium, and a major supplier of copper. The group has ambitious plans for 1997, targeting a 20 percent increase in nickel production to 213,000 tonnes from 177,185 tonnes in 1996.
